title: Cipolle Ripiene
subtitle: Baked onions stuffed with breadcrumbs, parmesan, and herbs
excerpt: Large onions are par-cooked, hollowed out, and filled with a savoury mix of their own flesh, breadcrumbs, parmesan, and fresh herbs. They bake until collapsing and golden. A dish that looks more involved than it is.
sourceNotes: Piedmontese stuffed onion tradition. Synthesised from regional recipes common to Cuneo and the Langhe area.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare and fill the onions up to 8 hours ahead. Keep covered in the fridge. Bake from cold, adding 5 to 10 minutes to the oven time.

content.text: These baked onions are a gentle, savoury starter or side. Use large onions that will hold their shape. The key watch-point is not to hollow them too thin or the sides will collapse during baking.
Heat the oven to 190C. Put the unpeeled onions in a large saucepan of salted water. Bring to the boil and cook for 15 minutes. Drain and leave until cool enough to handle.
Slice the top third off each onion and keep these as lids. Peel the skins away. Use a small spoon to hollow each onion, leaving two or three outer layers intact as a shell.
Finely chop the scooped-out onion flesh. Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the chopped flesh for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Tip into a bowl to cool.
Add the breadcrumbs, parmesan, beaten egg, parsley, thyme, nutmeg, salt, and pepper to the bowl. Mix until the filling holds together.
Spoon the filling into the onion shells. Mound it slightly. Set the lids on at an angle. Place the onions in the roasting tin.
Dot each onion with a little butter. Add a splash of water to the tin to stop them scorching.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the onions are tender through and the filling is golden on top. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The onion shells collapse in the oven.
items.cause: Too much flesh was removed during hollowing.
items.fix: Leave at least two firm outer layers intact. Prop the onions close together in the tin so they support each other.

items.symptom: The filling is dry and crumbly.
items.cause: Not enough egg or the cooked onion was too dry.
items.fix: Add a tablespoon of olive oil or a second beaten egg to the filling before stuffing.

items.symptom: The bases are scorching before the tops colour.
items.cause: The tin has no liquid and the heat is too direct.
items.fix: Add 3 to 4 tablespoons of water to the tin and cover loosely with foil for the first 15 minutes.
